title: NDPS special courts - how trial timelines actually work
p1:
A drug case can move slowly even when the law creates a special court for it.

Many people assume “special court” means instant trial and quick judgment. But the reality is more complex.
p2:
NDPS Special Courts are designed to handle offences under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act with focused attention. However, a special court does not remove every step of a criminal trial.

Evidence collection, forensic reports, witness appearances, cross-examination, and legal challenges can all affect the timeline. A surprising fact: even a strong case may take years if key witnesses do not appear or scientific evidence is delayed.
p3:
The practical takeaway is that trial speed depends not only on the court but also on how efficiently every stage moves. The purpose of a special court is better management of NDPS cases, not bypassing basic legal safeguards.

Knowing this difference helps explain why some cases conclude quickly while others continue for a long time.
conclusion: What do you think affects NDPS trial delays the most — court procedures, evidence issues, or repeated adjournments?
